round_summary:
{
  "round_analysis": {
    "summary": "Round 0 diagnostic exploration confirms MFCC-based spectral-envelope features as the strongest standalone family for sarcasm detection. The only candidate to improve over the MFCC-20 baseline is MFCC-20 with delta/delta-delta (pipeline 1, +0.0104 F1). All non-MFCC families—pitch, energy, spectral contrast, and their combinations—performed substantially below baseline when used alone, suggesting prosodic summary statistics in isolation lack discriminative power under this fixed SVM configuration. A controlled MFCC-13 vs MFCC-20 comparison shows the higher-order coefficients (14–20) contribute meaningful signal (+0.015 F1), and adding temporal dynamics via deltas yields a further +0.010 gain, pointing toward richer MFCC representations as the most promising direction.",

    "hypothesis_result": {
      "status": "partially_supported",
      "reason": "The hypothesis aimed to identify which primitive acoustic directions—spectral shape, energy, pitch, temporal statistics—are most informative relative to a minimal MFCC baseline. Design fidelity holds: each candidate tested a distinct feature family with appropriate aggregation. The outcome clearly ranks spectral-envelope (MFCC) features highest, with delta dynamics adding value, but the hypothesis that prosodic cues (pitch, energy) would carry useful standalone sarcasm signal is not supported. The diagnostic goal of ranking feature families was achieved, but only one direction (MFCC+deltas) showed improvement, so the breadth of 'multiple informative directions' part is not supported."
    },

    "key_findings": [
      "Controlled MFCC depth comparison (MFCC-13 at 26-dim vs MFCC-20 at 40-dim, both mean/std aggregation): MFCC-20 outperforms MFCC-13 by +0.015 F1 (0.701 vs 0.686), indicating coefficients 14–20 carry non-redundant spectral detail useful for sarcasm discrimination under RBF SVM with gamma=0.0065. The dimensionality increase from 26 to 40 does not hurt despite the small dataset.",
      "Controlled static-vs-dynamic comparison (MFCC-20 mean/std 40-dim vs MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta mean/std 120-dim): adding delta and delta-delta features improves F1 by +0.010 (0.701→0.712), suggesting frame-to-frame temporal dynamics of the spectral envelope encode sarcasm-relevant prosodic modulation that static summary statistics miss. The 3× dimensionality increase (40→120) does not cause overfitting on 690 samples, possibly because the RBF kernel with low gamma tolerates moderate-dimensional inputs.",
      "Pitch alone (F0 summary stats, 9-dim) scored worst at 0.583 (−0.118 vs baseline), while energy alone (RMS stats, 8-dim) scored 0.640 (−0.061). Combining pitch+energy into a 9-dim vector (0.635, −0.066) performed slightly worse than energy alone, suggesting the pitch component may introduce noise or that the reduced energy aggregation (4 features vs 8) lost information. The combination is not additive.",
      "Spectral contrast (14-dim, 0.654, −0.048 vs baseline) outperformed both pitch and energy families but still fell well short of MFCCs, indicating that peak-valley spectral structure captures some timbral signal but is a much weaker standalone representation than the full cepstral envelope.",
      "All non-MFCC candidates have much lower dimensionality (8–14) than the baseline (40). The fixed RBF SVM gamma=0.0065 was likely tuned for 40-dim input; lower-dim features produce a different effective kernel bandwidth, which is a confounder for interpreting their absolute F1 values as pure feature-quality measures."
    ],

    "positive_signals": [
      "candidate cand01_mfcc20_delta: MFCC family; 20 MFCCs + delta + delta-delta with mean/std aggregation yielding 120-dim output; +0.0104 F1 vs baseline (0.712 vs 0.701); temporal dynamics of the spectral envelope likely capture prosodic modulation patterns (pitch and energy contour changes encoded implicitly in MFCC trajectories) that static mean/std summaries discard."
    ],

    "negative_signals": [
      "candidate cand02_pitch_prosody: pitch/F0 family; pyin F0 with 9 summary stats (mean/std/min/max/range/median/skew/kurtosis/voiced_fraction) yielding 9-dim; −0.118 F1 vs baseline; F0 summary statistics alone are too coarse and low-dimensional to discriminate sarcasm, possibly because sarcasm's pitch signature is in contour shape rather than global statistics, and zero-fill for unvoiced frames adds noise.",
      "candidate cand03_energy_envelope: energy/RMS family; frame-level RMS with 8 summary stats (mean/std/min/max/range/skew/kurtosis/max-to-mean ratio) yielding 8-dim; −0.061 F1 vs baseline; energy dynamics alone carry weak sarcasm signal, though outperforming pitch suggests loudness variation is slightly more discriminative than pitch level.",
      "candidate cand04_spectral_contrast: spectral contrast family; 7-band librosa spectral_contrast with mean/std aggregation yielding 14-dim; −0.048 F1 vs baseline; spectral contrast captures some timbral information but is substantially redundant with MFCCs since both encode spectral shape, and the lower dimensionality under-represents the signal.",
      "candidate cand05_mfcc13_meanstd: MFCC family; 13 MFCCs with mean/std yielding 26-dim; −0.015 F1 vs baseline; dropping coefficients 14–20 loses useful higher-order spectral detail, confirming these coefficients carry non-trivial sarcasm-relevant information.",
      "candidate cand06_pitch_energy_combined: combined pitch+energy family; F0 (5 stats) + RMS (4 stats) yielding 9-dim; −0.066 F1 vs baseline; combining two weak prosodic families does not produce additive benefit; the reduced aggregation for each component compared to their standalone versions may lose information, and the low dimensionality remains a handicap."
    ],

    "redundant_or_duplicate_strategies": [
      "cand06_pitch_energy_combined partially overlaps with cand02_pitch_prosody and cand03_energy_envelope: the pitch component uses a subset of F0 stats (5 of 9) and the energy component uses a subset of RMS stats (4 of 8). The combined candidate's result (0.635) falling between pitch-alone (0.583) and energy-alone (0.640) is consistent with it being a compressed union rather than an independent test. Its metric should not be treated as fully independent evidence from cand02 and cand03."
    ],

    "uncertainties": [
      "No fold-level variance is reported; with 690 samples in 5-fold CV, individual fold variance could be substantial. The +0.010 improvement for MFCC+deltas may not be statistically significant.",
      "The fixed RBF SVM hyperparameters (C=1.6, gamma=0.0065) were presumably tuned for the 40-dim MFCC-20 baseline. Gamma controls the effective kernel bandwidth relative to feature dimensionality; candidates with 8–14 dimensions may be disadvantaged by a gamma that is too small for their scale, while the 120-dim delta candidate may benefit from gamma being relatively larger in its space. This confounds feature-quality comparisons across different dimensionalities.",
      "Pitch extraction via pyin may produce many NaN/unvoiced frames for short utterances or noisy TV audio; the zero-fill fallback strategy could severely distort F0 statistics, making it unclear whether the poor pitch performance reflects weak signal or implementation artifact.",
      "All candidates use the same sample rate, windowing (25ms/10ms hop), and librosa defaults; any systematic audio loading issues (e.g., sample rate mismatch) would affect all pipelines uniformly but could suppress absolute performance."
    ],

    "leads_from_this_round": [
      "MFCC-delta depth lead: MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta at 120-dim was the best candidate; a natural next probe is whether richer aggregation of the same 60 frame-level features (e.g., adding percentiles, slope, or range to mean/std) could capture more prosodic contour information without increasing the number of MFCC coefficients.",
      "MFCC coefficient count lead: MFCC-13 < MFCC-20 suggests higher-order coefficients help; testing MFCC-25 or MFCC-30 with mean/std would reveal whether additional coefficients continue to help or overfit.",
      "MFCC+prosody fusion lead: since MFCC+deltas (spectral dynamics) scored best and prosodic features (pitch, energy) scored poorly alone, concatenating MFCC-20 mean/std with a small set of F0/energy stats could test whether prosodic features add complementary signal when combined with a strong spectral backbone rather than standing alone.",
      "Aggregation richness lead: all round-0 candidates used mean/std (or basic summary stats); testing percentile-based or segment-level aggregation (e.g., first-half vs second-half statistics) on MFCC-20 could capture temporal contour asymmetry relevant to sarcasm without requiring delta coefficients.",
      "Gamma-dimensionality confounder lead: the low-dim prosodic features may have been disadvantaged by the fixed gamma; a controlled test pairing low-dim features with a gamma rescaled by dimensionality ratio would disambiguate feature quality from kernel mismatch—though this requires model changes outside current scope, awareness of this confounder should temper negative conclusions about pitch/energy families."
    ]
  }
}

{
  "round_analysis": {
    "summary": "Round 1 tested six refinement/exploration directions around the MFCC-delta backbone. The strongest result is cand11 (MFCC-20 static with rich 7-stat aggregation, 140-dim, F1=0.729, +0.028 vs baseline, +0.018 vs history_best), which surpassed even the MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta mean/std best from Round 0. Rich aggregation on static MFCCs was the dominant factor; adding deltas on top of rich aggregation (cand13, 300-dim) or appending prosodic features (cand15, 138-dim) still beat the baseline but did not match cand11. Extending MFCCs to 25 (cand12), temporal segmentation (cand14), and standalone spectral shape descriptors (cand16) all failed to improve over history_best. The hypothesis is partially supported: richer aggregation and fusion refinements did improve over baseline, but extending coefficient count and temporal halves did not, and the exploratory spectral candidate strongly underperformed.",

    "hypothesis_result": {
      "status": "partially_supported",
      "reason": "Design fidelity is adequate: the six candidates map to the six intended directions (rich aggregation, extended MFCC count, MFCC+prosody fusion, temporal segmentation, and two spectral explorations collapsed into one spectral-shape ensemble plus the rich-agg variants). Outcome: richer aggregation (cand11) produced the largest gain (+0.028 vs baseline), confirming this was an untapped direction. However, the MFCC-25 extension (cand12, -0.006 vs history_best) and temporal halves (cand14, -0.010 vs history_best) failed, and the spectral shape exploration (cand16, -0.086 vs baseline) strongly underperformed. MFCC+prosody fusion (cand15) showed only modest uplift (+0.008 vs history_best), suggesting prosodic features add marginal complementary signal. Overall, 3 of 6 directions beat history_best but only the rich-aggregation direction showed a substantial lift."
    },

    "key_findings": [
      "Controlled comparison — rich aggregation vs deltas for capturing temporal dynamics: cand11 (MFCC-20 static, 7-stat aggregation, 140-dim, F1=0.729) outperformed cand13 (MFCC-20+delta+dd, 5-stat aggregation, 300-dim, F1=0.724) by +0.006 and the Round-0 best MFCC-20+delta+dd mean/std (120-dim, F1≈0.712) by +0.018. This suggests that higher-order summary statistics (min, max, median, skew, kurtosis) over static MFCCs capture distributional information that partially substitutes for explicit delta features, and that the 300-dim representation in cand13 may suffer from curse-of-dimensionality with the fixed RBF SVM gamma=0.0065.",
      "Controlled comparison — MFCC-20 vs MFCC-25 with same delta/mean-std pipeline: cand12 (MFCC-25+delta+dd, 150-dim, F1=0.705) scored -0.006 vs history_best (MFCC-20+delta+dd, 120-dim, F1≈0.712), indicating that coefficients 21–25 introduce noise that degrades the RBF SVM under fixed hyperparameters. The marginal spectral detail in higher cepstral coefficients is not useful for sarcasm detection at this sample size.",
      "Controlled comparison — temporal segmentation vs global aggregation: cand14 (MFCC-20 first/second half mean/std, 80-dim, F1=0.701) was essentially tied with the baseline (40-dim, F1≈0.701, delta +0.0001). Doubling dimensionality by splitting into halves did not help, suggesting either sarcastic prosody lacks systematic temporal asymmetry in this corpus or that a two-segment split is too coarse to capture it.",
      "Feature-family interpretation — prosodic supplement: cand15 (MFCC-20+delta+dd + F0/RMS stats, 138-dim, F1=0.720) gained +0.008 vs history_best (MFCC-20+delta+dd, 120-dim). The 18 additional prosodic dimensions contributed a small but positive increment, consistent with F0/energy being individually weak (Round 0) but carrying some complementary signal when anchored to a strong MFCC backbone.",
      "Feature-family interpretation — spectral shape descriptors: cand16 (centroid/bandwidth/rolloff/flatness, 16-dim, F1=0.615) underperformed baseline by -0.086, even worse than Round-0's spectral contrast (14-dim, F1≈0.654). The low dimensionality (16-dim) compounds with the fixed gamma=0.0065, but the magnitude of the deficit suggests these global spectral-shape descriptors carry very little sarcasm-discriminative information standalone."
    ],

    "positive_signals": [
      "cand11_mfcc20_rich_agg: MFCC-20 static with mean/std/min/max/median/skew/kurtosis aggregation, 140-dim, F1=0.729, +0.028 vs baseline, +0.018 vs history_best; higher-order distribution statistics (skew, kurtosis, extremes) over MFCC trajectories may encode voice-quality modulation and spectral variation patterns characteristic of sarcastic delivery without requiring explicit delta computation.",
      "cand13_mfcc20_delta_rich_agg: MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta with mean/std/median/Q10/Q90 aggregation, 300-dim, F1=0.724, +0.022 vs baseline, +0.012 vs history_best; percentile-based aggregation on delta features captures tail behavior of temporal dynamics, though the 300-dim representation appears suboptimal under fixed gamma.",
      "cand15_mfcc20_delta_plus_prosody: MFCC-20+delta+dd mean/std concatenated with F0 and RMS summary stats, 138-dim, F1=0.720, +0.019 vs baseline, +0.008 vs history_best; prosodic features provide a small complementary signal (pitch contour variability, energy dynamics) on top of the MFCC backbone that spectral-envelope features alone do not fully capture."
    ],

    "negative_signals": [
      "cand12_mfcc25_delta_meanstd: MFCC-25+delta+delta-delta mean/std, 150-dim, F1=0.705, -0.006 vs history_best (MFCC-20+delta+dd, 120-dim); coefficients 21–25 likely capture high-frequency noise or speaker-specific spectral details that do not generalize for sarcasm detection with 690 samples.",
      "cand14_mfcc20_temporal_halves: MFCC-20 mean/std split by first/second half, 80-dim, F1=0.701, +0.0001 vs baseline (effectively zero gain); a binary temporal split does not surface sarcasm-relevant prosodic dynamics, and the doubled dimensionality without new information dilutes discriminability.",
      "cand16_spectral_shape_ensemble: Spectral centroid/bandwidth/rolloff/flatness with mean/std/skew/kurtosis, 16-dim, F1=0.615, -0.086 vs baseline; these coarse spectral descriptors are largely redundant with information already encoded in lower MFCCs and lack the fine spectral-envelope resolution needed for sarcasm cues."
    ],

    "redundant_or_duplicate_strategies": [
      "cand14_mfcc20_temporal_halves partially overlaps with baseline_mfcc20_meanstd: both compute mean/std of MFCC-20; cand14 splits frames into halves but the whole-utterance means of the two halves average to approximately the global mean. The near-zero delta (+0.0001) is consistent with this near-redundancy. It should not be treated as independent evidence that temporal segmentation is informative."
    ],

    "uncertainties": [
      "No fold-level variance is reported for any candidate; with 690 samples in 5-fold CV, the standard error of F1 is likely ≥0.01–0.02, so deltas below ~0.015 (e.g., cand12 at +0.004 vs baseline, cand14 at +0.0001, cand15 at +0.008 vs history_best) may not be statistically significant.",
      "The fixed RBF SVM gamma=0.0065 strongly favors a specific effective feature-scale range. The 300-dim cand13 and 150-dim cand12 may be disadvantaged not because their features are poor but because gamma is suboptimal for those dimensionalities. Conversely, cand11's 140-dim may be in a sweet spot for the fixed hyperparameters.",
      "Skew and kurtosis in cand11's aggregation can be numerically unstable for very short utterances; if some utterances have few frames, these statistics may contain outlier values that coincidentally help the SVM decision boundary rather than capturing genuine signal.",
      "Shared implementation assumptions: all candidates use default librosa settings for MFCC extraction (sr=22050, n_fft=2048, hop_length=512). Any audio loading or resampling inconsistencies affect all candidates equally and are not detectable from the gradient alone."
    ],

    "leads_from_this_round": [
      "Rich-aggregation depth lead: cand11 used 7 statistics on static MFCC-20 (140-dim) and achieved the best result. A controlled test could combine rich aggregation with delta/delta-delta features at a reduced aggregation set (e.g., mean/std/skew/kurtosis only, to keep dimensionality moderate around 160–200 dim) to test whether deltas add signal on top of rich aggregation without the dimensionality penalty seen in cand13's 300-dim.",
      "Rich-aggregation + prosody fusion lead: cand11 (rich agg, 140-dim, F1=0.729) and cand15 (MFCC+delta+prosody, 138-dim, F1=0.720) both beat history_best through different mechanisms—distributional statistics vs. prosodic supplement. Combining rich aggregation on static MFCC-20 with F0/RMS summary stats (~158-dim) could test whether both gains are additive.",
      "Aggregation ablation lead: cand11 used 7 statistics but the individual contribution of skew/kurtosis vs. min/max/median is unknown. A controlled ablation comparing subsets (e.g., mean/std/min/max vs. mean/std/skew/kurtosis) on MFCC-20 could identify which statistics carry the sarcasm-discriminative signal, potentially yielding a more compact and robust feature set.",
      "Finer temporal segmentation lead: cand14's binary temporal split showed no gain, but a finer approach (e.g., thirds or a slope/regression coefficient of MFCC trajectories over time) could capture temporal dynamics differently from deltas, testing whether temporal modulation matters in a form that the coarse two-segment split missed."
    ]
  }
}

{
  "round_analysis": {
    "summary": "Round 2 tested four directions: aggregation ablation, delta enrichment, prosodic fusion, and temporal regression on top of the Round 1 best (cand11, 140-dim rich-agg, F1=0.729). Three enrichment strategies (cand23, cand24, cand26) exceeded history best, with spectral contrast fusion (cand26, 154-dim, F1=0.738) producing the largest gain at +0.009 vs history best. The aggregation ablation revealed that min/max/median statistics (cand21) carry substantially more discriminative signal than skew/kurtosis (cand22), but neither subset alone matches the full 7-stat set. Temporal regression (cand25) was clearly harmful. The 0.729 ceiling was broken, but gains are small and significance is unknown without fold-level variance.",

    "hypothesis_result": {
      "status": "partially_supported",
      "reason": "The hypothesis had four sub-goals. (1) Aggregation ablation was properly executed and showed that min/max/median are more load-bearing than skew/kurtosis, but both contribute — supported. (2) Delta enrichment at moderate dim (cand23, 180-dim) produced a small gain (+0.003 vs history best) — weakly supported, though the delta may be within noise. (3) Prosodic fusion (cand24, 153-dim) and spectral contrast fusion (cand26, 154-dim) both showed positive enrichment — supported. (4) Temporal regression slope/curvature (cand25) performed worse than even the baseline — not supported. The overall claim that 0.729 could be pushed further is supported by three candidates exceeding it, but the claim that this would reveal which aggregation components are dispensable was partially answered: neither skew/kurtosis nor min/max/median is individually dispensable."
    },

    "key_findings": [
      "Controlled aggregation ablation comparison: cand21 (mean/std/min/max/median, 100-dim, F1=0.715) vs cand22 (mean/std/skew/kurtosis, 80-dim, F1=0.701) shows min/max/median contribute +0.013 over baseline while skew/kurtosis contribute ~0. However, the full 7-stat set (cand11, 0.729) outperforms both ablations, indicating a synergistic interaction between range statistics and higher-order moments — skew/kurtosis may need the min/max context to be useful, possibly because kurtosis identifies peaky MFCC distributions only when the range anchors the scale.",
      "Controlled enrichment comparison at matched dimensionality: cand24 (140 MFCC + 13 prosody = 153-dim, F1=0.734) vs cand26 (140 MFCC + 14 spectral contrast = 154-dim, F1=0.738). Nearly identical backbone and output dimension, yet spectral contrast outperforms prosody by +0.004. This suggests sub-band timbral texture (peak-valley structure) is more complementary to cepstral-envelope features than F0/energy summary, consistent with MFCC already partially encoding energy and F0 information through the lower cepstral coefficients.",
      "Delta enrichment (cand23, +40 delta dims = 180 total, F1=0.732) underperformed both prosody fusion (cand24, 153-dim, F1=0.734) and spectral contrast fusion (cand26, 154-dim, F1=0.738) despite having more dimensions. This suggests that at 180-dim, the fixed gamma=0.0065 starts to penalize the added dimensions more than the delta information compensates, or that mean/std delta aggregation is too coarse to capture the temporal dynamics that matter.",
      "Temporal regression features (cand25, slope+curvature, 80-dim, F1=0.689) performed -0.013 below baseline. The linear and quadratic regression coefficients may be dominated by noise in short utterances or may average out the rapid modulations that carry sarcasm signal, effectively producing a lossy low-pass summary of temporal dynamics that discards the distributional information mean/std retains."
    ],

    "positive_signals": [
      "cand26_rich_agg_plus_spectral_contrast: MFCC-20 (librosa defaults) 7-stat aggregation (140-dim) + 7-band spectral contrast mean/std (14-dim) = 154-dim total; F1=0.738, +0.036 vs baseline, +0.009 vs history best; spectral contrast's peak-valley sub-band structure likely encodes harmonic-to-noise timbral variation complementary to the smooth cepstral envelope captured by MFCCs.",
      "cand24_rich_agg_plus_prosody: MFCC-20 7-stat (140-dim) + F0 pyin 6-stat+voiced_fraction (7-dim) + RMS 6-stat (6-dim) = 153-dim; F1=0.734, +0.032 vs baseline, +0.004 vs history best; prosodic contour summary provides modest complementary signal, though F0/energy may partially overlap with lower MFCCs.",
      "cand23_rich_agg_plus_delta_compact: MFCC-20 static 7-stat (140-dim) + delta MFCC-20 mean/std (40-dim) = 180-dim; F1=0.732, +0.031 vs baseline, +0.003 vs history best; delta features add marginal temporal-dynamics information, though the gain is small and may be offset by dimensionality cost at fixed gamma."
    ],

    "negative_signals": [
      "cand25_mfcc_temporal_regression: MFCC-20 mean/std (40-dim) + per-coefficient linear slope (20-dim) + quadratic curvature (20-dim) = 80-dim; F1=0.689, -0.013 vs baseline, -0.041 vs history best; regression-based temporal summarization likely discards frame-level distributional variation that mean/std retains, and short utterances may produce numerically unreliable slope/curvature estimates that add noise rather than signal.",
      "cand22_agg_ablation_moments: MFCC-20 mean/std/skew/kurtosis (80-dim); F1=0.701, -0.00002 vs baseline, -0.028 vs history best; skew and kurtosis alone (without min/max/median context) provide essentially zero gain over baseline mean/std, suggesting these higher-order moments are only useful in conjunction with range statistics that anchor the distributional shape."
    ],

    "redundant_or_duplicate_strategies": [
      "cand22_agg_ablation_moments (F1=0.701) is near-identical in performance to the baseline (F1=0.701, delta=-0.00002). The mean/std component dominates the 80-dim feature space and the added skew/kurtosis dimensions contribute nothing in isolation. This should not be treated as independent evidence that skew/kurtosis are useful — only their synergistic contribution within the full 7-stat set (cand11) demonstrates value."
    ],

    "uncertainties": [
      "No fold-level variance is available for any candidate. The top three candidates (cand26=0.738, cand24=0.734, cand23=0.732) span only 0.006 F1 and all gains vs history best are ≤0.009; these differences may be within noise of 5-fold CV on 690 samples.",
      "Fixed RBF SVM gamma=0.0065 creates a dimensionality-dependent confounder: the effective kernel bandwidth changes with feature count, potentially penalizing higher-dimensional representations regardless of information content. The 180-dim cand23 underperforming 154-dim cand26 may reflect this confound rather than feature quality.",
      "All enrichment candidates share the same 140-dim MFCC rich-agg backbone. Their performance differences (0.732–0.738) reflect only the marginal contribution of 14–40 supplementary dimensions, making these comparisons especially sensitive to scaling interactions and noise.",
      "Feature standardization scope and implementation (e.g., whether spectral contrast, F0, and MFCC features are scaled jointly or independently, and whether scaler is fit per fold) could affect relative feature influence in the RBF kernel and is not controlled across candidates.",
      "cand25's temporal regression requires minimum 3 frames for quadratic fit; the handling of very short utterances (fallback behavior) is unverified and could introduce systematic artifacts."
    ],

    "leads_from_this_round": [
      "Spectral contrast enrichment lead: cand26 (MFCC-20 rich-agg + spectral contrast mean/std, 154-dim) is the new best at 0.738. Applying richer aggregation (e.g., 5–7 stats) to the spectral contrast features could increase their contribution while staying under ~170-dim, testing whether spectral contrast carries distributional information beyond mean/std.",
      "Multi-enrichment fusion lead: cand24 (prosody) and cand26 (spectral contrast) both show positive signal as supplements to the MFCC backbone. A triple fusion of MFCC-20 rich-agg + spectral contrast + compact prosody could test whether these two complementary families are additive, though total dimensionality (~160–170) must be managed.",
      "Aggregation synergy lead: the ablation showed min/max/median (cand21, 100-dim, 0.715) >> skew/kurtosis (cand22, 80-dim, 0.701), yet the full 7-stat (cand11, 140-dim, 0.729) exceeds both. A controlled test of mean/std/min/max/median + just kurtosis (dropping skew, 120-dim) could identify whether kurtosis alone provides the synergistic interaction, potentially allowing a more compact backbone.",
      "Delta aggregation richness lead: cand23 used only mean/std for deltas (40-dim), yielding a modest +0.003 gain. Applying richer aggregation (e.g., mean/std/min/max/median) to deltas at 100-dim, combined with a compacted static backbone (~100–120 dim), could test whether delta distributional shape matters while keeping total dim ~200–220.",
      "Spectral contrast aggregation lead: the standalone spectral contrast was weak in Round 0 (F1=0.654) but the mean/std enrichment in cand26 was the strongest supplement (+0.009 vs history best). Testing spectral contrast with richer per-band aggregation (min/max/skew/kurtosis) could amplify the timbral signal while the MFCC backbone provides the primary discriminative structure."
    ]
  }
}

{
  "round_analysis": {
    "summary": "Round 3 produced a new history best (cand31, F1=0.7438) by enriching spectral contrast aggregation from mean/std to 5-stat, confirming spectral contrast as the strongest supplement family. However, triple fusion with prosody did not exceed richer spectral contrast alone, delta MFCC with alternative aggregation collapsed at 200-dim, and chroma proved a weak supplement. The skew-ablation candidate confirmed skew is dispensable in the MFCC backbone aggregation. The overall pattern reinforces that spectral contrast enrichment is the most productive direction, while dimensionality above ~175 is penalized under fixed gamma=0.0065.",

    "hypothesis_result": {
      "status": "partially_supported",
      "reason": "Sub-hypothesis (a) supported: richer spectral contrast aggregation (5-stat, 35-dim) improved over mean/std (14-dim), yielding new best F1=0.7438 (+0.006 vs history best). Sub-hypothesis (b) not supported: triple fusion (cand32 at 0.7422, cand36 at 0.7395) did not exceed spectral-contrast-only supplement (cand31 at 0.7438), suggesting prosody adds redundant or noisy dimensions. Sub-hypothesis (c) partially supported: dropping skew (cand33, 134-dim, F1=0.7378) produced negligible loss (-0.00007 vs history best), confirming skew is dispensable. Sub-hypothesis (d) not supported: alternative delta aggregation (cand34, 200-dim, F1=0.7019) collapsed to near-baseline, dominated by the 200-dim penalty. Sub-hypothesis (e) not supported: chroma (cand35, 164-dim, F1=0.7293) was -0.008 vs history best, indicating harmonic/tonal features do not carry sarcasm-discriminative signal."
    },

    "key_findings": [
      "Controlled comparison: spectral contrast 5-stat (cand31, 175-dim, F1=0.7438) vs spectral contrast mean/std (cand26, 154-dim, F1=0.738) shows +0.006 gain from adding min/max/median per band. The additional 21 dimensions capturing sub-band timbral extremes and central tendency provide net-positive information despite the dimensionality cost, suggesting that the peak-valley distributional shape across frequency bands encodes sarcasm-relevant timbral variation beyond mean level and spread.",
      "Controlled comparison: triple fusion cand32 (SC mean/std + prosody 9-dim, 163-dim, F1=0.7422) vs cand26 (SC mean/std only, 154-dim, F1=0.738) shows +0.004; but cand31 (SC 5-stat only, 175-dim, F1=0.7438) exceeds both.
